title: Mentor handshake: 10-day activation & infra access checklist (temp-to-perm pilot)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, execution-first checklist to run a 10-day mentor handshake for incoming contract hires on the temp-to-perm pilot. Goal: get a new engineer productive on core infra (GPU pools, test clusters, private-deploy sandboxes) and capture evidence for conversion decisions.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: People Ops partnering with Eng Managers, Platform, Security, and assigned mentor (peer-level engineer).
- Scope: first 10 calendar days (Day 0 through Day 9) plus conversion-evidence capture to feed 30/60/90 review. Not a full 90d playbook; this is the rapid activation slice for infra-heavy roles.

Before Day 0 (owner: People Ops + Hiring Manager) 
- Confirm offer and contract terms (People Ops).
- Pre-create SSO account + Slack + Google group (IT ticket template: IT-ACCESS-NEWUSER).
- Request baseline access: AWS read-only, dev VPC, internal docs, and repo view. Securely collect 2FA device preference.
- Hardware signoff: arrange loaner dev machine if onboard is remote (Infra Ops).
- GPU pool access request: open ticket to infra-reqs with model: role, expected vGPU type, ctrs per week. Include expected seq lengths and batch needs. (Owner: Manager).
- Send welcome packet with first-week agenda + mentor intro + playbook link.

Day 0 checklist (owner: Manager + Mentor)
- Morning: Manager 30-min welcome (context, high-level roadmap, expectations).
- Mentor handshake: 45-min pair intro + micro-goals doc (see template below). Mentor should: provide repo map, local run script, and one reproduction of the team’s dev/test run.
- Access validation: walk through SSO, VPN, AWS console, GitHub, internal artifact registry. Resolve any blocked tickets.
- Quick infra orientation: one-pager on GPU queues, quotas, and how to request burst capacity. (Mentor/Infra).
- Set 10-day objectives and measurable acceptance criteria in a shared doc.

Days 1–3: bootstrapping and small wins (owner: Mentor)
- Day 1: Run local dev loop: clone, install, run unit tests. Deliverable: successful end-to-end inference on a toy model in dev environment.
- Day 2: Submit small PR that touches infra config (e.g., modest doc update or test harness tweak). Review time boxed to 24 hours.
- Day 3: Run a controlled job on the staging GPU pool with mentor present (observe KV cache behavior, batching quick-check). Confirm cost/latency telemetry visible in Console.

Days 4–7: deeper integration (owner: Mentor + Manager)
- Assign an owner for an infra troubleshooting ticket (e.g., latency spike reproducible). Candidate to triage, write hypothesis, and propose next steps.
- Introduce rollout policy and canary deploy process used by the team. Candidate to script a canary with safe rollback (demo with mentor).
- Security quick training: KMS usage, secrets rotation, least-privilege patterns required for private deployments.

Days 8–9: evidence capture & conversion prep (owner: Manager + People Ops)
- Fill conversion rubric (see rubric text). Manager and mentor add notes, link to PRs, logs, and trace artifacts.
- Candidate self-reflection: 15-min note on blockers, next growth steps, and confidence score (1–5).
- Schedule 30/60/90 sync and explain conversion timeline.

Mentor handshake specifics (how to run the 45-min session)
- Before session: mentor pre-read doc (5–10 min) listing three recommended starter tasks, repo pointers, and critical slack channels.
- 0–10 min: intro + role expectations + clarity on 'what success looks like' for 10 days.
- 10–30 min: guided dev onboarding — run the main test script together until green. Take notes in checklist.
- 30–40 min: infra access demo — show GPU pool dashboard, where to check job health, and how to fetch logs.
- 40–45 min: quick 3-item growth plan and next 24h priorities.

Conversion interview rubric (temp->perm evidence, owner: Manager + Mentor)
- This is intentionally lightweight: 4 evidence buckets, each scored 0/1/2. Requirement to pass: total >=6 and no zero in "collaboration".
  - Technical competence (code quality, infra understanding): 0=not demonstrated, 1=basic, 2=solid.
  - Delivery (PRs, triages, task ownership): 0=missed, 1=delivered with heavy help, 2=independent delivery.
  - Collaboration (peer reviews, communication, mentorship): 0=poor, 1=adequate, 2=clear collaborator.
  - Security & Ops hygiene (secrets, least-privilege, rollback plan): 0=unsafe/missed, 1=some measures, 2=proactive.

Sample interview evidence to collect:
- Links to 1–3 PRs with reviewer comments.
- Staging job trace showing successful run and relevant Console telemetry.
- Mentor note on day-to-day communication and blocker response time.
- Candidate self-reflection note (15–30 lines).

Scoring and timeline
- Fill rubric by Day 9. If candidate meets threshold, schedule 30d formal review (perm conversation) at Day 30. If borderline, extend to Day 60 with targeted growth plan. If fail, offboard per contract.

Early success metrics (signals we monitor)
- Time to first green end-to-end run (target <= 48 hours).
- First non-doc PR merged (target <= 72 hours after Day 0).
- Mentor NPS (quick thumbs survey) average >= 4/5.
- No high-severity security findings in first 30 days.

Ticket and request templates (copy/paste)
- Infra access: "Infra-REQ: New temp hire. Name: {name}, Role: {role}, GPU-type: {type}, Start: {date}, Quota: {vCPU/vRAM}, Purpose: onboarding tests"
- KMS key request: "KMS-PROVISION: Project {proj}, Purpose: staging-run-keys, TTL: 90d"

Onboarding artifacts to attach to rubric:
- PR links (string list), staging run IDs, mentor note snippet, security training completion (screenshot).

Quick mentor checklist (to tick)
- [ ] Intro + agenda sent before day 0
- [ ] Repo map + local run script provided
- [ ] First green run observed together
- [ ] Small PR merged
- [ ] Staging job executed
- [ ] Conversion rubric filled

Mentee checklist (to tick)
- [ ] Confirmed SSO / Slack / GitHub access
- [ ] Completed security micro-training module
- [ ] Ran local dev loop and posted results
- [ ] Opened at least one PR
- [ ] Submitted self-reflection note

Open questions / known risks
- Burst GPU quota requests can take >72h in some regions — pre-request earlier for roles that need it.
- Private deployments require HSM/KMS onboarding which is slow if customer-managed; coordinate with Security earlier.
- Need clarity on whether contract hires get long-lived service accounts — legal to advise. (Action: People Ops to confirm with Security/Legal).

Next steps (owners: People Ops, Platform, Security)
- People Ops: iterate this doc with Legal to clarify SA lifetime policy.
- Platform: template ticket to pre-allocate small vGPU pool for onboarding windows.
- Security: prepare a one-page HSM/KMS FAQ for temp hires.

Appendix: quick evidence template (copy into rubric doc)
- PR1: URL
- PR2: URL
- Staging run ID: run-2025-08-15-xx
- Mentor note (2–4 lines): "
  - Strengths: 
  - Gaps: 
  - Recommendation: convert/extend/offboard"

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep rubric intentionally low-friction; hiring managers hate heavy admin in week 1.
- This grew out of infra onboarding pain where hires were blocked on GPU access. Pilot with 3 teams (serving-runtime, platform-engineering, private-deployments).
- Post-pilot retrospective after 6 hires.

TODOs

- [Platform] create infra-req prefill for temp hires (due 2025-08-22).
- [Legal] confirm temp hire access constraints (sync 2025-08-19).

References / links
- Confluence: onboarding-temp-to-perm-v2
- Jira: PEOPLE-3187 (temp->perm pilot)
- Slack thread: #people-ops-onboard (see pinned)

End.
